claim: On 03 FEB 2023 about 8:54 p.m., eastbound Norfolk Southern train 32N derailed 38 freight cars at milepost 49.5 in East Palestine, Ohio
source_quote: On February 3, 2023, about 8:54 p.m., eastbound Norfolk Southern Railway (NS) train 32N derailed 38 mixed freight railcars at milepost 49.5

claim: The train had 3 locomotives and 149 cars, weighed 17,977 tons and was 9,309 feet long
source_quote: the train weighed 17,977 tons and was 9,309 feet long
note: p. 4; about 1.76 miles. The spec title "Thirty-Mile Train" is wrong

claim: At 7:37 p.m. the Sebring HBD (MP 79.8) read the failing bearing at 38°F above ambient; no alert or alarm
source_quote: At 7:37 p.m., train 32N passed over an HBD at MP 79.8 in Sebring, Ohio. The HBD recorded a temperature 38°F above ambient
note: p. 5; "The bearing temperatures did not result in any alert or alarm."

claim: Surveillance cameras in Salem showed a fire on wheelset 1 of the hopper car
source_quote: The images showed a fire on wheelset #1 of the hopper car.

claim: At 8:13 p.m. the Salem HBD (MP 69.01) read the L1 bearing at 103°F above ambient
source_quote: The HBD recorded a temperature 103°F above ambient on the L1 bearing of the hopper car

claim: NS's non-critical alert threshold was 90°F above ambient
source_quote: temperature exceeding NS's 90°F above-ambient threshold for a non-critical alert

claim: 103°F was below the 170°F threshold that would have broadcast an alarm to the crew; the crew did not know
source_quote: This measurement was below the 170°F threshold that would have triggered an alarm broadcast to the train crew, which remained unaware that a bearing was showing unusual behavior.

claim: The Salem alert went to a desk, not to the crew
source_quote: did not broadcast an alarm to the train's crew

claim: The desk analyst did not see the Salem alert while on higher-priority alerts; seeing it would not have prevented the derailment
source_quote: immediately seeing the Salem HBD alert would not have prevented the derailment

claim: At East Palestine the train was doing about 43 mph; the limit was 50 mph
source_quote: Locomotive event recorder data showed the train was traveling about 43 mph. The maximum authorized speed in the area was 50 mph.

claim: The East Palestine HBD read 253°F above ambient and broadcast a critical alarm
source_quote: this HBD recorded a temperature 253°F above ambient on
note: p. 7; "The HBD immediately transmitted a critical alarm."

claim: 253°F was more than 50°F above the critical alarm threshold
source_quote: Its exterior temperature measurement had reached at least 253°F, more than 50°F above the critical bearing alarm threshold.

claim: The next detector after Salem was about 19 miles away
source_quote: by the time the train reached the next HBD, about 19 miles away in East Palestine, the L1 bearing was already failing

claim: The bearing separated less than a minute after the alarm, as the crew began to stop
source_quote: The bearing separated less than a minute later, as the crew began to stop the train.

claim: The crew's train handling and response to the alarm did not contribute (finding 1)
source_quote: the train crew's proper train handling and appropriate response to the bearing alarm and derailment

claim: The bearing went from below the alert threshold to separated in about 30 miles
source_quote: the bearing that led to the derailment went from below the alert threshold to separated in about 30 miles

claim: The Salem alert did not reflect the true temperature of the bearing (finding 4)
source_quote: did not reflect the true temperature and failing condition of the L1 wheel bearing

claim: NS procedures (monitor only on a non-critical alert), detector limits and spacing did not give the crew adequate warning (finding 6)
source_quote: did not give the train's crew adequate warning to stop the train before the suspect bearing failed and caused the derailment

claim: Why the bearing failed is not known: the fire erased the evidence
source_quote: the root cause of the bearing's failure remains unclear
note: p. 111; answers the "$7 tube of grease" belief

claim: The heat erased traces of fatigue, loss of lubrication or water ingress
source_quote: were erased by the high temperatures of the burn-off and subsequent fire exposure

claim: NS did not inspect the hopper car; it was added at the TRRA yard
source_quote: NS did not inspect the hopper car relevant to the East Palestine derailment because it had been added to the train in the TRRA yard

claim: Insufficient evidence whether the TRRA inspection missed signs of failure (finding 3)
source_quote: There is insufficient evidence to determine if the Terminal Railroad

claim: The AAR definition of an overheated bearing is based on what makes a repair billable to the car's owner
source_quote: the AAR definition of an overheated bearing is based on what makes a railcar repair billable to the railcar owner or lessor
note: p. 106; testimony of the AAR SVP

claim: Railroads choose thresholds balancing preventing bearing failures against avoiding unnecessary stops
source_quote: balancing between preventing bearing failures and avoiding unnecessary stops

claim: AAR Rule 36 defines an overheated bearing as at least 170 degrees above ambient
source_quote: an overheated bearing is defined as measured by a wayside detector at least 170 degrees above ambient temperature
note: hearing day 2, 23 JUN 2023, p. 214, NTSB question

claim: AAR witness: the thresholds are in the car repair billing rules
source_quote: Those are thresholds in AAR's car repair billing rules which authorize the ability of a railroad to take a car out of service

claim: AAR witness: thresholds too low cause a lot of false stops
source_quote: if you put the thresholds too low, you're going to have a lot of false stops

claim: NTSB asked if the thresholds are a standard for removal and billing; the AAR answered "Correct."
source_quote: they are a standard at which bearings can be removed from service and billing and the car owners could be billed for it? MR. RUSH: Correct.

claim: AAR witness: it is in the operating railroad's interest not to have derailments from hot bearings
source_quote: it's in the interest of the operating railroad not to have derailments attributable to hot bearings
note: p. 216; the other side, always beside C26–C28

claim: Post-accident checks found FRA-reportable defects on 26% of the non-derailed cars, all inspected by NS or TRRA
source_quote: identified FRA-reportable defects on 26% of the railcars, all of which had received NS or TRRA mechanical inspections

claim: An NS senior general foreman email appeared to state a 90-second inspection target per car
source_quote: appearing to state a target time of 90 seconds for both inbound and outbound railcars

claim: The NTSB could not determine whether inspection time goals contributed
source_quote: does not support a determination of whether mechanical inspection time goals contributed

claim: The NTSB opened a special investigation into NS organization and safety culture in March 2023
source_quote: In March 2023, the NTSB announced that we would conduct a special investigation of NS's organization and safety culture.
note: p. 87; status of its report to check

claim: A 1-mile evacuation zone affected about 2,000 residents
source_quote: Emergency responders established a 1-mile evacuation zone that affected about 2,000 residents.

claim: The incident commander did not know of the shipper's dissenting opinions
source_quote: The incident commander was not aware of dissenting opinions the VCM shipper had provided to NS and its contractors.

claim: A contractor hired by NS breached the five VCM cars at 4:37 p.m. on 06 FEB 2023
source_quote: A contractor hired by NS breached the VCM tank cars at 4:37 p.m. on February 6

claim: The vent and burn was not necessary to prevent a polymerization explosion
source_quote: The vent and burn procedure was not necessary to prevent a polymerization-induced explosion.

claim: No injuries were reported in the derailment or response
source_quote: No injuries were reported during the derailment or emergency response.

claim: Phasing out DOT-111 cars early is feasible but unlikely because of economic and business disincentives (finding 19)
source_quote: such action is unlikely because of economic and business disincentives

claim: DOT-111 cars in flammable liquids service must be gone by 01 MAY 2029
source_quote: by May 1, 2029, tank cars transporting flammable liquids must meet the newer DOT-117 specification

claim: The FRA found cost and lease rates a disincentive to phase out DOT-111 cars faster
source_quote: provided a disincentive for tank car owners and shippers to phase out DOT-111 cars faster than required

claim: Probable cause: the L1 bearing on the 23rd car overheated and the axle separated
source_quote: the failure of the L1 bearing on the 23rd railcar in the consist that overheated and caused the axle to separate

claim: On 11 FEB 2019 NS announced a plan targeting a 60 percent operating ratio by 2021
source_quote: targeting an operating ratio of 60 percent by 2021

claim: NS said it was implementing precision scheduled railroading
source_quote: As we implement precision scheduled railroading

claim: The plan continued share repurchases using free cash flow and borrowing capacity
source_quote: continuance of share repurchases using free cash flow and borrowing capacity

claim: The same plan named working safely among five principles
source_quote: serving our customers, managing our assets, controlling our costs, working safely, and developing our people

claim: NS's 2018 operating ratio was 65.4 percent
source_quote: our 2018 operating ratio of 65.4 percent

claim: NS averaged 30,456 employees in 2015 and 24,587 in 2019
source_quote: Average number of employees 24,587 26,662 27,110 28,044 30,456

claim: NS averaged 18,900 employees in 2022
source_quote: We employed an average of 18,900 employees during 2022

claim: NS share repurchases were $1,439 million in 2020
source_quote: Share repurchases ( 7 ) ( 59 ) ( 1,373 ) ( 1,439 )

claim: NS share repurchases were $3,110 million in 2022
source_quote: Share repurchases ( 13 ) ( 108 ) ( 2,989 ) ( 3,110 )

claim: The 2020 executive annual incentive was based on operating ratio and operating income
source_quote: payable based on our performance relative to pre-determined performance measures for operating ratio and operating income
note: 2021 proxy (DEF 14A); check whether later years added safety

claim: The cab speakers broadcast: Critical alarm, critical alarm, critical alarm. Norfolk Southern milepost 49.8, track 1 hotbox, axle 101, south rail
source_quote: Critical alarm, critical alarm, critical alarm. Norfolk Southern milepost 49.8, track 1 hotbox, axle 101, south rail.
note: p. 8; captured by in-cab audio; shown as TEXT only, never as audio

claim: A critical alarm requires the crew to stop at once and inspect
source_quote: a critical alarm requires a train's crew to immediately stop the train and inspect the wheelset that triggered the alarm

claim: 253°F above ambient is the maximum that type of detector can read; the real temperature may have been higher
source_quote: A reading of 253°F above ambient is the maximum reading for the type of HBD installed at MP 49.81; the actual temperature may have been higher.

claim: The head end travelled about 1,160 feet and stopped 38 seconds after the emergency application
source_quote: The head-end locomotives then traveled about 1,160 feet before coming to a stop 38 seconds later.

claim: The first 911 call came at 8:56:49 p.m.
source_quote: received the first 911 call reporting a derailment, explosion, and fire at 8:56:49

claim: 48 agencies responded
source_quote: indicate that 48 agencies were involved in the emergency response

claim: The shipper, Oxy Vinyls, assessed a low probability of polymerization on the 6:00 p.m. call of 04 FEB
source_quote: Oxy Vinyls assessed a low probability of polymerization based on the observed PRD behavior

claim: Oxy Vinyls was not invited to the 06 FEB meetings
source_quote: Representatives from Oxy Vinyls were not present and had not been invited to attend.

claim: Norfolk Southern's chief executive was in the second, smaller meeting
source_quote: SRS personnel, including the chief executive officer of NS

claim: The incident commander was told he had 13 minutes to decide
source_quote: he had 13 minutes to decide whether to allow them to proceed with the vent and burn

claim: He was told 153–158°F would mean an uncontrolled polymerization reaction
source_quote: if the temperature in a tank car reached 153–158°F, the result would be an uncontrolled polymerization reaction

claim: The NTSB found that range in no written guidance consulted at the scene
source_quote: The NTSB did not find this temperature range in written guidance about VCM consulted at the scene

claim: The hottest car had fallen from about 138°F to about 126°F by the meetings
source_quote: the highest tank car temperatures had fallen from about 138°F the previous afternoon to about 126°F

claim: The charges went off at 4:37 p.m., so 3:00 p.m. was not a hard deadline
source_quote: indicating that 3:00 p.m. was not a hard deadline for the procedure

claim: The NTSB: NS and its contractors compromised the integrity of the decision by creating unwarranted urgency
source_quote: NS and its contractors compromised the integrity of the vent and burn decision by creating unwarranted urgency

claim: The incident commander said he bore the responsibility for the decision
source_quote: the incident commander said that he bore the responsibility for this decision

claim: NS recognised $1,116 million of incident expenses in 2023, net of $101 million insurance
source_quote: the Company has recognized $1,116 million of expenses for costs directly attributable to the Incident, which is presented net of $101 million in insurance recoveries

claim: NS incurred net incident expenses of $325 million in 2024, net of $650 million insurance
source_quote: we incurred net expenses of $325 million associated with the Incident

claim: In 2025 recoveries exceeded incident expenses by $254 million
source_quote: insurance and other recoveries that exceeded additional Incident-related expenses by $254 million

claim: The NTSB: the AAR definition relates to billing for repairs, not directly to safety or wayside detection
source_quote: it relates to billing for repairs, not directly to safety or wayside detection

claim: NS based its thresholds on its own experience with HBDs and AAR standards (NS testimony)
source_quote: NS based its alert and alarm temperature thresholds on its own experience with HBDs and AAR standards
note: p. 106; NS side, always with C23
